Subject: CAIQ mappings: assertion formatting & tenant-split clarification

Hi Kimberly (and team),

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As we prepare the CAIQ bundle for our internal review board, a couple of formatting/packaging questions came up that will affect how we ingest the artifacts into our GRC tool: 

1) Assertion format: Do you have an opinionated format you prefer for responses (CSV rows vs. single-sheet mapping vs. per-control PDF)? Our ingestion pipeline expects a control ID column (e.g., CCM_1.1), an assertion summary, and a link to an evidence artifact. If you can provide a single-file mapping with those columns it will save time on our side.

2) Tenant split: Our scope includes production tenants A and B. For controls that are tenant-specific (network segmentation, key access), do you plan to provide one artifact per-tenant, or a combined artifact with per-tenant sections? Our ingestion will accept either, but we need a clear delimiter or header so artifacts don't get misattributed.

3) Sampling: we may request live log snippets for a handful of controls (e.g., CCM_6.2, CCM_11.3). Can you confirm retention windows and whether you can produce redacted extracts on timestamps we provide?

If you can send a lightweight mapping stub and a brief note about tenant handling, we can confirm the minimal evidence set and drop a HubSpot ticket. 

Thanks,
Carter Liu
Security Director, Zenith Bank

Hi Carter — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a proposed packaging approach.

1) Assertion format: We typically deliver a single spreadsheet (XLSX) with these tabs: 
   - mapping (columns: CCM_ID, assertion_text, evidence_file, evidence_description, evidence_date, owner)
   - artifacts (list of files and redaction notes)
   - scope (explicit tenant entries and which services/exposed APIs they cover)

   I'll attach a stub named kim_caiq_mapping_v1.xlsx — that follows the mapping tab above. If you prefer CSV we can export.

2) Tenant split: For tenant-specific controls we will provide per-tenant artifacts as separate files when the evidence is materially different (e.g., tenant A firewall config vs tenant B). For shared artifacts (global key rotation policy, org-wide runbook) we'll include a combined artifact and clearly mark applicable tenants in the spreadsheet column "applicable_tenants".

3) Sampling / logs: We can produce redacted log extracts for specific date ranges. Retention for runtime telemetry is 90 days for the production clusters, with archived monthly snapshots going to our secure archive for 12 months. For the live snippets we will provide: redacted_stream_<control>_<tenant>.log.gz.

Proposed minimal deliverables for your ingestion pipeline:
- kim_caiq_mapping_v1.xlsx (mapping sheet populated)
- artifacts/ (zipped folder of evidence files named per CCM ID and tenant)
- runtime-log-sampler.tar.gz (contains small redacted extracts for requested controls)
- attestation-template.docx (for the on-record attestation we can sign)

If the above works, please confirm which CCM IDs you want as priority for sampling and the timestamp windows. We'll prepare the zipped bundle and a short README that maps file names to CCM IDs and tenants.

thanks,
Kimberly Park
